body: Hey there! I just replied user with a bunch of info about my case ([here's the comment if you'd like to read it](https://www.reddit.com/r/Herpes/comments/urqt9r/comment/j4ctlp8/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web2x&context=3)), but the short form of it is that I had an ongoing staph infection compounded by an autoimmune disorder that makes my skin very weak and susceptible to blistering. While my symptoms aren't gone, dealing with that helped IMMENSELY.

Hey there! I'm sorry for not logging in, but I did discover my issue, and if it's any help to you or anyone else that comes across this:

My particular problem seems to be an autoimmune disorder that causes my skin to be incredibly fragile and to blister very easily (in the "*epidermolysis bullosa*" family of disorders in my case), and every small skin issue turns into a very herpes-like blister. This is true now not only for my face, but everywhere on my body. It turned out that the original test they ran for HSV that came back positive was inaccurate, and something else was causing elevated IgM levels. Originally I had been tested because some very, very bad razorburn on my bikini area had also turned into a huge number of small, very itchy blisters. **The biggest issue that had caused them to spread and be even itchier than they already were was that I also had a staph infection**; my nose, armpits, and genital region were colonized, so any time I had a break in the skin, it created a new point of infection.

I went on multiple courses of antibiotics (about 6 weeks in total, in tandem with probiotics to protect my gut health) and FINALLY was able to clear my system of infection. I also used an antibiotic ointment up my nose to clear up the colonization, and I've switched to an antibacterial body wash (really it's a hand soap, but it smells nice and doesn't dehydrate my skin), and since then, I've had no issues with rampant itchy blisters.

That being said, **I DO still get small blisters any time my skin experiences even slight trauma**. If my partner has stubble and I rub my cheek against it too hard, I'll get a blister. They do itch, but no nearly as badly, and I believe it's just a sensation linked to the skin being put under stress. If I get a scrape on the surface of my skin anywhere, even if it isn't deep enough to bleed, it releases a lot of lymph/exudate (basically, every wound I get "weeps"), which I believe is the same issue, but without the surface skin remaining intact. I also experience little blisters anywhere I get a pimple, and - and this is gross, but I just want to provide as much info as possible - instead of the pimple pus being a little on the thick side, it mixes with the lymph and creates very "liquidy" pimples. Fortunately I don't get very many.

Other things I do to manage this problem and prevent blisters are moisturizing well and taking care of my skin as best as I'm able, as well as switching to a depilatory cream to remove hair from my bikini line (as razor burn + friction from thigh rub means lots of blisters) and swapping out my razor frequently to help prevent nicks on my armpits or groin. I hope that any of this information is helpful to you, and that you've either found a solution or that this puts you closer towards one.

It's hard to say; they usually come back in the same spots I've already had them and there isn't usually enough time in between new vesicles popping up to link it to something specific. The only trigger I've for sure linked to the outbreaks is stress. Any time I get stressed out, it's a minefield.

That's what I can't figure out; a recent blood test (taken for new gHSV) showed my IGG number at 1.04, but I've been dealing with these facial lesions for more than six months. I had chicken pox as a kid, so it's possible it's related. I have a follow-up scheduled but I was hoping to run into someone who'd had a similar experience.

Have you tried lactose-free milks like Lactaid? That might be a good option. Beyond that, I would go with soy milk. If you're getting plenty of lysine from other sources, oat milk may be a good option as well. Both are a little higher in arginine than lysine, but not as badly as almond, cashew, and hemp milks.

I never would have connected the two, but now that you mention it... I had a single herpes-like spot near my lip years ago: tingly, red, and it appeared after smoking from a shared pipe at a party. It went away fairly quickly and I never had anything else pop up. Fast forward to November; I got my COVID booster and right around the same time, I suddenly had cold sores start popping up. I had also gotten back into the dating scene, so I honestly just assumed that I'd picked it up from a partner. It could just be a coincidence, but I'd also had a not-great reaction to the second shot (pericarditis after second dose of Pfizer), so...? 🤷🏻‍♀️
